note: The group's subject is `--input.txs` handling at London: the new `.rlp` EIP-2718 form, and the pre-existing JSON-array form continuing to work there. Before this revision the group held 45 `.rlp` cases and a single JSON-form case, so the JSON path at `--state.fork=London` rested on one type-0 transaction. The 8 added cases give the JSON form two accepted type-0, two accepted and two rejected type-1, and two type-2 transactions (one accepted, one rejected for maxFeePerGas < baseFee). The type-2 pair is the same signed transaction as the `.rlp` variants in `london-fee-market`, re-presented field by field in geth's `txJSON` spelling, so the two input forms must produce the identical post state. A further 10 cases come from London *blockchain*-test fixtures via mkbc8n.py: a block header pins `transactionsTrie` and `receiptTrie`, so these are the only cases in the step that compare `txRoot` and `receiptsRoot` by value on a non-empty block -- everywhere else those two fields are only checked for shape, or against the empty-trie constant. They do not declare `stateRoot`, because the header's state root includes the 2 ETH block reward and the graded interface fixes `--state.reward=-1`; each case says so in its own `case.json`. The last 12 cases are `frontier/validation/transaction/bad_v_r_s` at London, one per transaction type times four out-of-range signature shapes. The JSON input path rejects the whole file for these, which is why `mkcorpus.py` skips them when building the inherited JSON corpora; the RLP path accepts the file and reports the transaction in `rejected[]`, so this is where sender recovery from a bad signature is actually observable. REQUIREMENTS.md section 3 already said they lived here; before this revision they did not.
